Clean all tanks and their lids with soap and water, and then thoroughly rinse with DI water. Then wipe or rinse the internal surfaces of the tanks with 6 % HNO3. An polyester cloth is suitable for contact with 6 % HNO3 at room temperature. After the acid treatment, thoroughly rinse all internal surfaces of the tanks at least 3 times with DI water. Use a minimum of 20 liters deionized water in each rinse. This procedure is designed for use with one acid soak tank and two deionized (DI) water tanks. The tanks and all utensils placed in contact with the cleaning solutions must be polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester or a poly-perfluorocarbon (i.e. Teflon). Solution contact or contamination with metals must be rigorously avoided.

record.field:
Soak
Solvent HF,HNO3, DI water
Concentration 2.3 wt% HF, 2.8 wt% HNO3
Balance DI water
Duration 30 / 90 minutes
Soak the quartz chamber in the 2.3 % HF, 2.8 % HNO3 acid tank at 25º C. Soak for 90 minutes if the chamber is contaminated with visible process residue. Soak for 30 minutes if the chamber has been flame polished by ASM and is undergoing a final acid clean before being returned to the customer for use in the tool. Empty all trapped air from inside the chamber to insure that the acid solution contacts all surfaces of the chamber.
A transition in the color of the acid from colorless to yellow, orange, or red indicates the formation of significant amounts of NO2 in solution. If this color change occurs, chamber processing should be immediately terminated, and the acid solution allowed to sit under the hood until the NO2 gas dissipates and the liquid returns to a colorless condition.

div.root:
Soak
Solvent HF,HNO3, DI water
Concentration 2.3 wt% HF, 2.8 wt% HNO3
Balance DI water
Duration 30 / 90 minutes
Soak the quartz chamber in the 2.3 % HF, 2.8 % HNO3 acid tank at 25º C. Soak for 90 minutes if the chamber is contaminated with visible process residue. Soak for 30 minutes if the chamber has been flame polished by ASM and is undergoing a final acid clean before being returned to the customer for use in the tool. Empty all trapped air from inside the chamber to insure that the acid solution contacts all surfaces of the chamber.
A transition in the color of the acid from colorless to yellow, orange, or red indicates the formation of significant amounts of NO2 in solution. If this color change occurs, chamber processing should be immediately terminated, and the acid solution allowed to sit under the hood until the NO2 gas dissipates and the liquid returns to a colorless condition.
